Four ways to parse the same line

The same one-line record is parsed in four languages. The interesting part is how each one reports a malformed field.

Python

def parse(line):
    name, value = line.split("=", 1)
    return name.strip(), int(value)

Rust

fn parse(line: &str) -> Option<(&str, i64)> {
    let (name, value) = line.split_once('=')?;
    Some((name.trim(), value.trim().parse().ok()?))
}

Shell

while IFS='=' read -r name value; do
  printf '%s -> %s\n' "$name" "$value"
done < records.txt

Diff

-old_name = value
+new_name = value

Each version keeps the trailing space out of the parsed value, which is the one rule the four implementations share.
